study_focus: Handle text using String and StringBuilder
domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers primitives, wrapper classes, operators, parentheses, type promotion, type casting, text handling with String and StringBuilder classes, and local variable type inference including usage as lambda parameters within Java SE applications.

This domain focuses on controlling program execution using loops, if/else conditional structures, and switch statements to direct logical flow within Java SE applications according to official Oracle requirements.

study_focus: Initialize objects with initializers and constructors
domain_guidance.summary: This domain explores object lifecycles, nested classes, instance members, static members, overloaded methods, instance initializers, static initializer statements, and object initialization constructors required for developing proper object-oriented Java SE applications.

This domain deals with error management via try/catch/finally blocks, try-with-resource statements, multi-catch clauses, and custom exceptions to ensure reliable exception handling across enterprise Java SE software deployment projects.

This domain addresses generics, wildcards, Java arrays, List collections, Set collections, Map collections, Deque collections, convenience methods, and sorting data using Comparator and Comparable interfaces for efficient data structures.

study_focus: Use Java Streams to filter and process data
domain_guidance.summary: This domain involves functional interfaces, lambda expressions from the java.util.function package, data processing with Java Streams, filtering, transformation, decomposition, reduction, grouping, and partitioning on sequential and parallel streams.

This domain covers the Java Platform Module System, automatic modules, declaring modules, using modules, exposing modules, service usage, and modular application deployment and execution for modern Java platform architectures.

study_focus: Create worker threads using Runnable and Callable
Develop thread-safe code using locking mechanisms
domain_guidance.summary: This domain focuses on worker threads using Runnable and Callable, managing concurrency using ExecutorService and the java.util.concurrent API, and developing thread-safe code utilizing different locking mechanisms for high-performance applications.

study_focus: Read and write console and file data
Handle file system objects using java.nio.file API
domain_guidance.summary: This domain addresses reading and writing console and file data using I/O Streams, implementing serialization and deserialization techniques on Java objects, and handling file system objects using the java.nio.file API.

study_focus: Develop code that mitigates security threats
Secure resource access and manage policies
domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers mitigation of security threats like denial of service, code injection, input validation, data integrity assurance, secure resource access for filesystems, policy management, and execution of privileged code.

study_focus: Connect to and perform database SQL operations
Process query results using JDBC API
domain_guidance.summary: This specific domain focuses heavily on connecting to databases, performing SQL operations, and processing query results using the JDBC API to build database-driven Java SE enterprise applications successfully without issues.

study_focus: Implement Localization using Locale and resource bundles
Parse and format messages, dates, and numbers
domain_guidance.summary: This specific domain explores localization through Locale objects, resource bundles, and Java APIs designed carefully to parse and format messages, dates, and numbers for international software deployment across global markets.

study_focus: Process annotations during execution and compilation
domain_guidance.summary: This specific domain involves creating custom annotations, applying annotations within Java code structures, and processing annotations dynamically during application execution and compilation phases according to official language specifications.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Manage your 90-minute limit carefully across all 50 questions during the exam. Read multiple select prompts completely to ensure all correct options are selected before submitting.

faq.answer_text: The certification exam consists of exactly 50 multiple choice and multiple select questions administered in a linear format by official Oracle testing centers for candidates.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: Candidates taking this certification test must achieve a minimum passing score of 68 in order to successfully earn the Java SE 11 Developer credential from Oracle.
The total exam duration is 90 minutes, providing candidates with adequate time to read and answer all 50 questions included in the test format during their session.
The registration fee for taking this certification exam costs $245 USD. Always check with Oracle for any details regarding future certification paths or registration updates.

editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the Java SE 11 Developer 1Z0-819 exam with detailed domain breakdowns, pricing, passing score, and study guidance from Oracle.

methodology.summary: This reference page aggregates official facts, domain breakdowns, and structural constraints gathered directly from official Oracle documentation sources and certification landing pages for developers.

editorial.overview: The Java SE 11 Developer 1Z0-819 certification exam validates your core programming abilities, object-oriented design principles, modular applications, concurrency, database access, and secure coding practices. Certified by Oracle, this linear format test consists of 50 questions with a passing score of 68 and a total duration of 90 minutes for all candidates taking the examination.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the official Java SE 11 documentation and study specifications. Practice writing code covering all thirteen domains, paying close attention to lambda expressions, modular applications, concurrency utilities, and secure coding practices to prepare for the 50 multiple choice and multiple select questions on the test.
editorial.who_should_take: Java developers and professional software engineers with hands-on experience building applications on the Java platform who are seeking formal credentialing of their technical competence through Oracle examinations.

exam_rules: Closed-book. No notes or reference materials. On-screen calculator for applicable exams. Proctor monitors throughout.
id_requirements: One valid government-issued photo ID with full name. Name must match Pearson VUE registration exactly.

lifecycle.summary: Oracle's MyLearn exam page is titled 'Exam 1Z0-819: Java SE 11 Developer [Retires November 30, 2026]' and its overview opens 'Important Update: This Certification exam will retire on November 30, 2026.' The exam is still bookable (Proctored Online, 90 minutes, 50 questions, 68% passing) and still earns 'Oracle Certified Professional: Java SE 11 Developer'. Oracle names no successor for it on that page.

recommended_experience: They have also exhibited thorough and broad knowledge of the Java programming language, coding practices and utilization of new features incorporated into Java SE 11.
renewal_options: Oracle certifications are version-specific. When Oracle releases a new database/platform version, a new exam version is typically released. Previous certifications remain valid as earned.

retake_policy.notes: 14-day waiting period after failed attempt. Maximum 3 attempts per exam in a 12-month period. Full exam fee required for each retake.

target_audience: Candidates who hold this certification have demonstrated proficiency in Java (Standard Edition) software development recognized by a wide range of world-wide industries.
